current_episode.title: The future of tokenisation: What 100 asset managers told us

guest.bio_context: Tom Bennett serves as Global Head of Fintech at Apex Digital, participating in a joint interview alongside Angie Walker, Global Head of Commercialization for Apex Digital. Angie Walker joined Apex one year prior to the recording and oversaw growth from 31 projects in flight to 557 projects within that single year. The two were interviewed by host Brian in connection with a tokenization survey report produced in partnership with Mergermarket, covering 100 senior managers across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC.

context.real_quote: Distribution is king. Everything we do is actually all about distribution — whether that's distribution onto a chain or multiple chains, distribution to a centralized digital venue, a decentralized digital venue, or to an aggregator.

pending_qa.q: What is the current scale of real-world asset tokenization globally, and how fast is it growing?
pending_qa.r: According to Angie Walker, global tokenization of real-world assets has just exceeded approximately $25 billion across the RWA community. US Treasuries alone have grown by 500% in less than two years. She describes this as a 'perfect storm moment' driven by existing investors expanding private market holdings, new DeFi-native investors, and demand for broader, always-on access to assets.

pending_qa.q: What is the generational gap between traditional fund investors and active digital wallet investors, and why does it matter for tokenization?
pending_qa.r: Angie Walker highlights that the average traditional fund investor is in their early 50s, while the average active retail investor in DeFi is around 27 years old — roughly half the age. This gap matters because younger investors expect 24/7 always-on access, real-time portfolio visibility, high yield diversity, and much greater control over their investments, creating urgent demand for tokenized, digitally native investment products.

pending_qa.q: How much wealth is expected to transfer to younger generations over the next two decades, and what does this mean for tokenized assets?
pending_qa.r: Angie Walker states that $124 trillion will be passed down through the generations over the coming two decades. She argues this will drive demand for broader access to quality assets such as private markets at a much earlier age, and that the recipients — who predominantly hold digital wallets — will expect to invest in a fundamentally different, digitally native way.

pending_qa.q: What are the primary drivers of tokenization adoption according to the 100 asset managers surveyed?
pending_qa.r: Among the 100 senior managers surveyed, 42% cited broadening investor access as the primary driver for tokenization, placing it far ahead of improved operational efficiency and cost reduction. This aligns with conversations Apex Digital is having with clients, where discussions have clearly shifted from operational efficiency gains toward expanding distribution and investor access.

pending_qa.q: What types of assets are currently being tokenized on the Apex Digital platform, and what emerging categories are gaining traction?
pending_qa.r: Apex Digital is tokenizing a diverse range of assets including real estate, private credit, venture capital, hedge funds, and SPVs. Angie Walker notes that tokenized funds now represent 60% of what Apex Digital does, with real estate and private credit being the two largest categories. Emerging areas include large-scale infrastructure 'giga projects' spanning multiple phases — such as commercial developments combining hotels, conference centers, and office complexes — as well as energy, oil, mining, and gas projects suited to multi-decade smart contract structures.

pending_qa.q: What is Apex Digital's Apex Invest platform and what scale has it reached?
pending_qa.r: Apex Invest is described as a marketplace designed to match fund managers with new types of investors. According to Tom Bennett, the platform currently has over 100 funds listed and hosts approximately $40 trillion of allocated capital, as reported by the product manager Nicholas. The platform provides a white-labeled capability for fund managers to access the wealth channel that is demanding private market products.

pending_qa.q: What is Apex Digital's track record in crypto fund administration, and what notable clients does it serve?
pending_qa.r: Angie Walker states that Apex has been doing crypto fund administration for 13 years and represents approximately 16% of all crypto fund administration globally. Notable clients include Coinbase Asset Management, for which Apex administers stable coin Bitcoin yield funds, and SkyBridge Capital. This activity is described as significant but rarely publicly discussed.

pending_qa.q: What is the significance of Apex Digital's role in launching the PhilQ fund by Fidelity International?
pending_qa.r: Angie Walker highlights that Apex Digital was part of the team that launched PhilQ, described as the first-ever triple-A rated liquidity fund rated by Moody's, launched by Fidelity International approximately one month before the recording. She states that capital being secured into that fund is growing very quickly and positions it as a landmark example of tokenized Treasury fund issuance.

pending_qa.q: How does Apex Digital's strategic partnership with LSEG enhance its distribution capabilities for tokenized funds?
pending_qa.r: Angie Walker describes LSEG — owner of Refinitiv — as a 'super strategic' partner, noting that LSEG has approximately 400,000 institutional investors on its platform. The partnership aims to integrate Apex's fund issuance services directly into LSEG's global wealth distribution platform, providing a level of distribution reach that Apex describes as unprecedented. Walker frames this as a key example of distribution being 'king' in the tokenization ecosystem.

pending_qa.q: How has Apex Digital's internal tokenization project pipeline grown over the past year?
pending_qa.r: Angie Walker reveals that when she joined Apex one year prior to the recording, there were 31 projects in flight at various stages including design, validation, and build. By the time of the interview, that number had grown to 557 projects — a growth of approximately 2,000% in one year. She attributes this to surging demand across both the traditional and digital asset sides of the business.

pending_qa.q: What infrastructure investments has Apex Digital made to support 24/7 tokenized Treasury operations?
pending_qa.r: To support always-on digital transfer agency capabilities, Apex Digital undertook a major infrastructure upgrade and opened new large-scale support centers in Hyderabad and other locations worldwide. The operating model was redesigned to include automated onboarding, automated KYC and AML processes, and scaled investor community management. Angie Walker describes this as a necessary response to the different velocity and cadence that tokenized Treasury services require compared to traditional fund administration.

pending_qa.q: What regulatory developments does Apex Digital see as catalysts for mainstream stable coin and tokenized Treasury adoption?
pending_qa.r: Angie Walker points to the Genius Act and the Clarity Act in the United States as regulatory frameworks expected to drive mainstream adoption of stable coins and money market funds. She argues that as these regulations mature, regulators around the world will come under pressure to align their own frameworks, accelerating global adoption. She also notes that tokenized Treasuries and money market funds are expected to become the largest single backer of stable coins outside of fiat currency.

pending_qa.q: What does the survey reveal about the internal organisational scale of tokenization teams within asset managers?
pending_qa.r: Tom Bennett observes that a few years ago, tokenization work within asset management firms was handled by a handful of people, often siloed in standalone innovation teams. The Apex-Mergermarket survey shows that tokenization teams have now scaled significantly, with staff from all parts of the business getting involved. He notes that while most S&P 500 firms and large financial institutions have digital innovation teams, the pool of people with the required skills and subject matter expertise is not growing at the same rate as demand, making external service providers increasingly critical.

pending_qa.q: What is the strategic rationale behind Apex Digital's acquisition of Tokenhive, and how does in-house technology ownership differ from third-party partnerships?
pending_qa.r: Tom Bennett explains that acquiring Tokenhive brought technology expertise in-house, allowing Apex Digital to design solutions from the inside rather than relying on third-party partnerships where influence over the technology roadmap is limited. He states that owning the business allows Apex to 'see where the puck is going' and design for future outcomes. He frames technology not as a product but as an enabler, and the in-house capability as critical to controlling the direction of the platform.
